grammar: noun; masculine/neuter depending on sense; context determines inflection

meanings.english: phenomenon; principle; teaching; Dhamma; quality or state
meanings.bangla: ধর্ম; নীতি; শিক্ষা; স্বভাব বা অবস্থা; প্রসঙ্গভেদে ধম্ম

note: A highly polysemous term. A research dictionary must preserve contextual senses rather than force one Bengali or English equivalent.

meanings.english: goodwill; benevolent friendliness; an attitude wishing welfare
meanings.bangla: মঙ্গলকামনা; কল্যাণমুখী সদিচ্ছা; সকলের হিতকামনাময় চিত্ত

note: The application should distinguish the lexical sense from later technical meditation instructions and their commentarial expansions.

meanings.english: suffering; unsatisfactoriness; painful or unreliable conditioned experience
meanings.bangla: দুঃখ; অসন্তোষজনকতা; পীড়াদায়ক বা অনির্ভরযোগ্য সংসারিক অভিজ্ঞতা

note: Its translation depends strongly on doctrinal and grammatical context; the Four Noble Truths use it in several related but distinguishable ways.
In the three-characteristic framework it is paired with dukkha and anattā as a mode of examining conditioned phenomena.

meanings.english: not-self; not an enduring self or essence
meanings.bangla: অনাত্ম; স্থায়ী আত্মা বা আত্মসত্তা নয় এমন

note: Avoid treating anattā as a simple metaphysical slogan; context, grammatical case and the object under examination matter.

meanings.english: Nibbāna; extinguishing/release; the unconditioned goal described in the early Buddhist path

note: The interface should link this headword to occurrences, doctrinal concepts, and commentarial discussions rather than provide only a one-line translation.

meanings.english: truth; reality; a true statement or principle
meanings.bangla: সত্য; বাস্তবতা; সত্য অবস্থা বা সত্যনীতি

note: In cattāri ariyasaccāni, the term is technical and should be read together with the fourfold structure and its tasks.
A research view should distinguish paññā as a broad faculty from its specific role in the noble path and threefold training.

meanings.bangla: শীল; নৈতিক আচরণ; সংযত ও শৃঙ্খলাবদ্ধ আচরণ

note: The database should eventually distinguish individual precepts, restraint, and higher-training contexts instead of treating every occurrence as identical.
Later data should connect occurrences to jhāna, samādhi training, and Abhidhamma/commentarial taxonomies.
The exact rendering depends on context; the research engine should eventually expose occurrences in the Satipaṭṭhāna and other frameworks side by side.
